title: Perfect Tense
definition: The German Perfekt is a common past tense used in everyday conversation to talk about completed actions. It is usually formed with haben or sein in the present tense plus a past participle (Partizip II) at the end of the clause.

rules.title: Basic structure
rules.explanation: Pattern: subject + conjugated haben/sein + other information + past participle.

rules.title: Regular past participles
rules.explanation: Many regular verbs form the participle with ge- + stem + -t. Verbs ending in -ieren do not use ge-.

rules.title: Irregular past participles
rules.explanation: Many common verbs have irregular participles ending in -en; learn them individually.

rules.title: haben or sein?
rules.explanation: Most verbs use haben. Many verbs expressing movement from one place to another or a change of state use sein, including gehen, fahren, kommen, werden, and aufstehen.

rules.title: Separable and inseparable verbs
rules.explanation: Separable verbs commonly place ge- between the prefix and stem (aufstehen → aufgestanden). Inseparable prefixes such as be-, ver-, er-, and ent- usually do not take ge-.

comparison.word_order: The participle goes at the end of the clause.

common_mistakes.explanation: Gehen usually takes sein in the Perfekt.
The conjugated auxiliary is in position two; the participle goes at the end.
Studieren forms the participle studiert without ge-.

mastery_goal: You can describe past events using haben or sein plus the correct participle and place the participle at the end.
